notes:
POC objective: validate Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive personalization + moderation pipeline. Primary success criteria: p95 generative latency < 120ms for small-context queries, sustained throughput >= 3k tokens/sec across peak shards, and stable GPU util >= 60% without tail spikes > 200ms.

Background: Oratorio runs a live highlights service that generates short video captions, personalized summaries and safety checks on user clips. Current infra: hybrid k8s + internal CPU GPU fleet; costs rising. Want predictable unit cost and clear fallback behavior during spikes.

POC scope (detailed):
- Representative prompts: mix of short system prompts (<=64 tokens) for moderation and reranking, and medium-context (<=1024 tokens) for highlight generation. Example seeds attached in Drive doc.
- Models: evaluate open variants (Redwood-verified) and quantized 32->8-bit flows; compare latency/quality delta.
- Load tests: incremental ramp to 1k concurrent requests (small payloads) then to 3k concurrent over 1 hour. Target sustained tokens/sec 3k at 95% latency target.
- Soak test: 72-hour continuous run at 70% of peak load to detect memory leaks, KV cache correctness, and degraded tail behaviors.
- Failure modes: simulate region outage and force fallback to compatible model variant; measure failover time and error rate.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tail error rate, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, batch sizes, KV cache hit ratio, end-to-end user-perceived latency (including CDN).
- Reserved GPU planning: baseline proposal 8x A100-80GB (dedicated pool) + burst capacity to 12 GPUs via autoscale policy. Preliminary estimate: 8 GPUs -> ~3.2k tokens/sec for our average payload; 12 GPUs -> headroom for 4.8k tokens/sec.

SLA/contract notes:
- Oratorio requests 99.95% uptime for dedicated endpoints and a latency SLO with credit-based remediation if p95 > target for two consecutive weeks. Legal asked for explicit credit calc tied to monthly recurring fee.
- Security: require customer-managed KMS, per-request audit logs, and EU data residency for EU-targeted users.
- Negotiation points: rollback windows for model updates, canary thresholds, and deterministic fallback chain.

Quotes/Call notes:
- CTO (A. Mehra): "We can't tolerate spikes >200ms during prime time; that breaks UX and retention."
- Head of ML infra: wants explicit guidance on prefix caching and batching config for our prompt mix.

- Mar wk3-4: Run load + soak tests; deliver performance report and tuning recommendations.
